Subject: Re: Kickoff: NovaHealth onboarding — SCIM & service-account notes

Hi Michael — a few technical clarifications ahead of the call. Quoting Dylan's asks below for context.

On SCIM attributes:
- Redwood expects: userName (email), givenName, familyName, displayName, active (boolean), and membership groups (groupMembers attribute). If you use Okta, the standard group claim works fine; in Azure AD we typically map the 'groups' claim via Graph.
- De-provisioning policy: we perform immediate user deprovision at SCIM 'active=false' by default unless you request a 24hr buffer.

Service-account pattern:
- We recommend 1 shared infra SA per environment (staging/prod) with scoped roles limited to inference-job:create and logs:read. If NovaHealth requires per-team SAs, we can support per-team provision via SCIM custom groups, but that adds lifecycle complexity.
- We will create the service accounts on our side and provide owner tags; you'll need to approve via your ticketing flow.

IP allowlist caveats:
- For staging, we'll allow the CIDR ranges you provide and add temporary entries for Redwood support IPs during dry-runs. Please note support IPs are time-limited and require a firewall exception ticket.

Attached: scim_attribute_map.csv (template). I'll paste a quick example here:
userName, givenName, familyName, displayName, active, groups
jane.doe@novahealth.com, Jane, Doe, Jane Doe, true, clinicians;analytics

If you can attach your SCIM export or sample Okta config beforehand, I will pre-populate these mappings.

— Irene
Irene Choi
Platform Engineer, Inference Integrations
Redwood Inference
Attachment: scim_attribute_map.csv (csv)
